# `silk/platform/native/clock`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Direct calls to the clocks of the system, for the native clock providers.

## When to use
`silk.system.system_clock_native` and `silk.system.monotonic_clock_native` use [`NativeClock`](#NativeClock). Application code uses
those providers through the `SystemClock` and `MonotonicClock` effects, so a test can replace
them.

## Details
Each read checks the result of the system. [`NativeClock.waitUntil`](#NativeClock.impl.waitUntil) keeps the same deadline
when a signal interrupts the wait, so the total wait does not grow.

## Gotchas
- A failed call or a bad result is a trap.
- A wait blocks the whole thread. It does not let another fiber run.
- A call fails to compile on targets other than WASI, Darwin on aarch64, and Linux with GNU libc on x86_64 or aarch64.

## Examples
### Read the clocks
```silk
import silk.platform.native.clock { NativeClock }
import silk.system.system_clock { SystemClock }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  // `true` selects the monotonic clock, `false` the system clock.
  let first = run NativeClock.now(true)
  let second = run NativeClock.now(true)
  if SystemClock.seconds(&second) < SystemClock.seconds(&first) {
    return 1
  }
  let resolution = run NativeClock.resolution(false)
  if resolution == 0 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `NativeClock` with `import silk.platform.native.clock { NativeClock }`.

The functions that read the system clocks and wait, for the native clock providers.

### When to use
`silk.system.system_clock_native` and `silk.system.monotonic_clock_native` use it. Application code uses those
providers through the `SystemClock` and `MonotonicClock` effects, so a test can replace them.

### Details
Each read checks the result of the system.

### Gotchas
- A failed call or a bad result is a trap.
- A wait blocks the whole thread. It does not let another fiber run.
- A call fails to compile on targets other than WASI, Darwin on aarch64, and Linux with GNU libc on x86_64 or aarch64.

<a id="NativeClock.impl.now"></a>

### Associated function `now`

```silk
pub effect fn now(monotonic: bool) -> Instant
```

Returns the time of the monotonic clock if `monotonic` is true, or of the system clock if it
is false.

A monotonic time is not negative. A failed call or a bad result is a trap.

<a id="NativeClock.impl.resolution"></a>

### Associated function `resolution`

```silk
pub effect fn resolution(monotonic: bool) -> u64
```

Returns the resolution of the selected clock, in nanoseconds. It is more than zero. A failed
call or a bad result is a trap.

<a id="NativeClock.impl.waitUntil"></a>

### Associated function `waitUntil`

```silk
pub effect fn waitUntil(when: Instant) -> ()
```

Blocks the thread until the monotonic clock reaches `when`.

#### Details
If a signal interrupts the wait, it waits again for the same deadline.

#### Gotchas
A negative deadline or a failed call is a trap. The wait does not let another fiber run.
